sources.title: Laya AI Model: How It Works, Run It Locally, and Evaluate It
sources.snippet: The Laya AI model is built for a particular kind of work: making a bounded decision about an input, then returning a structured answer and probabilities. Give it a support ticket, an email, a conversation, or a JSON state. Ask which queue should receive it, how urgent it is, or whether a stated condition is true. Laya answers those questions without writing a paragraph that your application ...

sources.title: Laya: replace your LLM-as-a-judge with a 322M-parameter decision engine
sources.snippet: Laya (26,000+ GitHub stars in 9 days) is a non-autoregressive System 1 decision engine: typed choice, score, and yes/no decisions over any text in a single forward pass, in 100+ languages. Install it, triage real support tickets, and add confidence-gated abstention — every step executed on CPU.

sources.title: Laya Judge: Ultra-Low Latency Local AI Agent Decisions
sources.snippet: Laya Judge offers ultra-low latency, local, and cost-free typed decisions for AI agents. Reduce LLM tokens, ensure data privacy, and integrate with oh-my-pi for confident judgment.

sources.title: Laya - AI Wiki | Wikiprompt
sources.snippet: Laya is an open-weight, non-autoregressive AI decision model released by the Indian startup Convai Innovations in September 2026 under the Apache 2.0 license. Like TypeSafe AI's closed Jev, it is a "System One" model: given a piece of state and typed questions it returns typed answers with calibrated probabilities instead of generating text, in a single forward pass of roughly 33 milliseconds ...
